messages:
From: Maya Patel <m.patel@cloudline.com>

Subject: Data residency + TTL / need deletion proof pack

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this -- Cloudline is preparing the security annex for our data processing agreement and security questionnaire. A couple of specific asks we need to close with our InfoSec team: 

1) Confirmation of where tenant data for Cloudline would be physically stored (region/zone) when using Redwood hosted API.
2) TTL / retention defaults for tokens, embeddings, and request logs; how those differ for ephemeral vs persisted workloads.
3) A sample erasure evidence package (audit log entries, S3 deletion markers, or runbook steps) we can show auditors.
4) Whether Redwood uses a customer-specific KMS or a shared key model, and how key deletion impacts data removal timelines.

If you can share a short pack (redacted ok) and a recommended statement we can include in the annex, that would be ideal. We have a legal deadline on Friday 11/05.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Security Program Manager
Cloudline Financial

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency + TTL / need deletion proof pack

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below and I’ll attach a short evidence pack for your reviewers. Ben and Kim are looped in for the runbook and logs.

1) Region: Hosted API defaults to the region selected at signup/tenant creation. For Cloudline (US), data is stored in us-west-2 by default; we can lock region with a contract addendum.

2) TTL / retention defaults: Request payloads (transient cache) are ephemeral (default KV TTL 48 hours for short-lived caching). Full request/response payloads are retained for diagnostic/quality purposes for 30 days by default and can be shortened to 0/7/14/30 on request. Embeddings and persistent artifacts are retained per tenant settings; default is 90 days unless you opt into longer-term storage. We’ll include the retention matrix in the pack.

3) Evidence pack: attaching a redwood_erasure_runbook_v1.pdf and a small s3-logs-sample.csv with deletion markers and corresponding audit entries. The runbook includes the deletion sequence and what auditors should expect to see in logs.

4) KMS: We support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS imported into your account (recommended for Cloudline). For hosted customers not providing CMK, we use per-tenant keys managed in our KMS account (separate keys per tenant). Key destruction is a separate SLA item: destroying a CMK you control will cryptographically render data unrecoverable immediately, but application-level deletion and backups still follow their retention/replication timelines.

Action items: Ben — can you confirm the backup retention/manifest timing we should include? Kim — can you paste the console link for the audit export (read-only)?

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if your auditors want a quick walkthrough.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

--

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Data residency + TTL / need deletion proof pack

Short update for the packet and auditor checklist:

- Backup retention: backups are incremental and have a retention of 7 days for ephemeral tiers, 30 days for standard tiers, and 90 days only if customer opts in. We have a documented backup manifest that shows deletion markers correlated to snapshot IDs.
- Deletion steps (high level): 1) API-level object deletion and KV purge; 2) manifest update + S3 delete markers; 3) background GC job clears shards; 4) backup snapshot expiry removes data per retention window.

I’m attaching a small csv with redacted S3 deletion markers and the log entries auditors typically look for. I’ll add a one-line summary to the annex language: "Redwood executes logical deletion within 24 hours of request and final snapshot expiry within configured backup retention window (default 7–90 days depending on tier)."

Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency + TTL / need deletion proof pack

Hi Maya — answering the three bullets inline and attaching a small diagram: 

• BYOK / HSM: Yes — we support BYOK where the customer’s KMS (AWS KMS with imported key material or CloudHSM-backed CMKs) is used. For hosted customers we can deploy a per-tenant key in a customer-owned AWS account; the key is HSM-backed if you provision CloudHSM/KMS with HSM protection. We’ll include the onboarding steps for establishing the CMK and the key policy snippet in the evidence pack.

• SLA for logical deletion: 
  - KV cache and prefix-level caches: cleared immediately on deletion request; you will see API-level confirmations within minutes.
  - Application-level logical deletion (object markers + manifest update): completed within 24 hours in >99% of cases.
  - Background GC and final snapshot expiration: follows backup retention windows (7–90 days depending on tier). Final permanent removal from immutable backups occurs at snapshot expiry.

• Evidence exports / attestations: We can provide a machine-readable CSV of audit entries (timestamp, actor, object-id, action, request-id) and a signed attestation PDF for the deletion event. The console link I pasted earlier is a read-only export for auditors.

Suggested DPA annex paragraph (feel free to reuse):

"Data deletion: Redwood Inference executes customer data logical deletions upon request. API-level object deletion and cache purges are performed immediately and confirmed by API response and audit log entries; background cleanup and final removal from backups occur according to the tenant’s configured backup retention window (default 7–90 days). For customers using customer-managed keys (CMK) with HSM protection, cryptographic destruction of the key will render stored ciphertext unrecoverable independent of backup retention. Redwood will provide deletion evidence (audit logs and deletion markers) upon request as set forth in the DPA."

Next steps: I’ll drop the attachments (runbook + diagram) to the shared drive link and send the CSV export; Ben, Kim — please confirm the export is the 11/01 sample we discussed.

If you’d like we can set a 20-minute sync with one of our engineers and an auditor on Wed.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
